> Part of the [AAN Training Program](../index.html) — **companion material
> for the federal AAN book series, not part of UIAO.**

Each [Track B module](../implementation-track.html) ends with labs; the
pages below stand up the environments those labs need. Scripts are embedded
in the pages (this repo's `docs/` tree is documentation-source only — copy
the blocks into your own shell/tenant).

## Lab tiers

| Tier | What it needs | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| **Tier F — fixture** | Nothing but this repo and Python | You want the evidence-binding mechanics (slot YAML → `uiao oscal ksi-ar`) without any cloud footprint |
| **Tier T — trial tenant** | A Microsoft 365 developer/trial tenant + Azure trial subscription | The PIM / Sentinel / Purview labs — full behavior, disposable blast radius |
| **Tier P — product eval** | A vendor eval (Infoblox/BlueCat) or containerized DNS/DHCP | The DDI lab's split-horizon and provisioning exercises |

## Safety rules (read before any lab)

1. **Never a production tenant.** Every lab assumes a disposable tenant or
   subscription you can delete. PIM changes, CA policies, and DLP
   enforcement are exactly the things that lock organizations out.
2. **Report-only first.** Where a lab creates a Conditional Access or DLP
   policy, it is created in report-only/simulation mode — the same
   discipline Books 07 and 09 mandate for production.
3. **Break-glass before lockdown.** The PIM lab creates its excluded
   emergency account *first*, mirroring Book 07's ordering.
4. **Teardown is part of the lab.** Each page ends with a teardown block;
   run it. Orphaned trial resources are how "labs" become shadow IT.

## Cost notes

- M365 E5 developer/trial tenants cover Entra ID P2 (PIM), Purview, and
  Defender features for the trial window.
- Sentinel bills per GB ingested — the lab keeps ingestion in the free-tier
  range by using a single VM/forwarder and seeded events.
- Infoblox/BlueCat evals are vendor-arranged; the Tier-F fixture path needs
  no license.

## Lab environment pages

| Page | Module | Stack | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| [DDI lab (Book 01)](lab-b1-ddi.html) | B1 | Infoblox eval or BIND/Kea containers + IPAM fixture | P / F |
| [PIM & privileged access lab (Book 07)](lab-b4-pim.html) | B4 | Entra ID P2, Intune, Graph PowerShell | T |
| [Sentinel detection lab (Books 08/10)](lab-b5-sentinel.html) | B5 | Log Analytics + Sentinel, one forwarder VM | T |
| [Purview data-protection lab (Book 09)](lab-b5-purview.html) | B5 | Purview labels/DLP, Key Vault Premium | T |

Modules B2 (SD-WAN/SASE) and B6 (continuity/SBOM/governance) intentionally
have no tenant page yet: B2 needs vendor SD-WAN gear or eval licenses
(track via the [vendor catalog](../vendor-training-catalog.html)), and
B6's labs are document- and CI-shaped (SBOM workflow on any repo, tabletop
exercise) — they run anywhere.

## The common final step — bind the evidence

Every lab ends the same way, regardless of tier: place the produced
artifact where a slot mapping can reference it, then regenerate verdicts:

```bash
uiao oscal ksi-ar --output exports/oscal/ksi-ar.json
```

The [Track A rubrics](../assessment-rubrics.html) score what you produce.
